learning_objective: 🎯 A picture is worth a thousand numbers! Learn how to turn boring data tables into beautiful, insightful line charts, bar graphs, and histograms using Matplotlib.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Matplotlib is a Python library for plotting 2D graphs. The `pyplot` module provides a MATLAB-like interface. We always import it as: `import matplotlib.pyplot as plt`.
Created using `plt.plot(x, y)`. It connects data points with straight lines. It is the best choice for showing trends over a continuous period of time (like stock prices or temperature).
Created using `plt.bar(x, y)`. It uses rectangular bars to compare different categories of data (like comparing sales of 4 different car brands). Use `plt.barh()` for horizontal bars.

Created using `plt.hist()`. It looks like a bar chart without spaces between bars. It is used to show the frequency distribution of a single continuous variable (like grouping students into height ranges: 150-160cm, 160-170cm).
A raw graph is confusing. You must add labels! `plt.title()` adds a heading. `plt.xlabel()` and `plt.ylabel()` label the axes. `plt.legend()` adds a box explaining what different colors mean.

fun_activity.title: 🌡️ The Weather Grapher
fun_activity.instructions: Take a piece of paper and plot Monday to Friday on the X-axis. Plot temperatures (20, 22, 25, 24, 21) on the Y-axis. Draw a dot for each day and connect them with a line. You just manually executed `plt.plot()`!

exam_tips: 📌 The most common mistake in practicals is forgetting `plt.show()`! Your graph will NOT appear on the screen unless you call this function at the very end.
📌 Be ready to differentiate between a Bar Chart and a Histogram: Bar charts compare discrete categories (with gaps), while Histograms show continuous frequency intervals (no gaps).
📌 To change the color of a line, pass the 'color' argument: `plt.plot(x, y, color='red')`.
quick_recap: ⭐ The X-axis is the horizontal line, and the Y-axis is the vertical line.
⭐ A Legend is crucial when you are plotting multiple lines on the exact same graph so the viewer can tell them apart.
⭐ Visualizing data makes it instantly easier to spot outliers, patterns, and trends that raw numbers hide.
